chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was brought the Jewess who had poisoned the sheep for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said to her: 'What carried you to do what you did?' She said: 'I said, if he is a Prophet, it would not harm him, and if he is a king, I relieved the people from him.' He said: 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned her.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) pardon the Jewess who poisoned him?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s magnanimity by pardoning the Jewish woman who poisoned the sheep, illustrating the principle of 'al-'afw' (pardon) over strict retribution. Her rationale—distinguishing between prophetic immunity and political authority—underscores the theological and social dimensions of his mission, while his forgiveness serves as a model for leadership in Shia ethics.
